captions.text: Business email compromise cost $3.05 billion in reported losses in 2025.
Now AP teams are adding AI agents, and the invoice can attack the agent.
Airlock assumes every invoice is hostile.
Airlock opens every invoice inside a disposable sandbox on Vultr.
One VM holds the keys. The gVisor sandbox VM holds nothing worth stealing.
The model that reads the raw invoice has no tools, and plain-code policy makes every decision.
Every sandbox: no network, no secrets, single use.
Six demo invoices on the live site: two clean, four attacks.
Each one opens in its own sandbox, six at a time.
Two cleared. Two blocked. Two quarantined.
Nothing reaches the ledger without a person.
A clean invoice from a known vendor.
The model doesn’t act on the invoice. It writes code to parse it.
Nine checks, recomputed outside the sandbox: totals, IBAN, three-way match.
Every sandbox run is a fresh container, destroyed after.
No network. Zero environment variables. Read-only root. gVisor runtime.
This is the parsing code the model wrote, run inside the sandbox.
Even a cleared invoice waits for a person.
Approved: posted to the ledger, and the evidence is signed.
Only human-approved invoices ever reach the ledger.
This invoice hides white-on-white text telling the AI to send out its environment and approve itself.
Even if the model is fooled, there are no secrets, no network and no approval tool. Blast radius: zero.
The hidden instructions, shown here as inert text.
Quarantined. A person reviews it, and nothing is paid.
This invoice says “pay here”, and links to a lookalike login page.
A browser opens it in its own sandbox, behind an egress proxy, and a vision model flags the credential harvest.
This is what the sandboxed browser saw.
The forced download is hashed and quarantined, never opened. It’s the EICAR test file.
The page’s CPU loop ran under a one-CPU cap, then the container was destroyed.
A “new bank account”, from orchardcl0ud: a lookalike domain with a zero.
Blocked by plain-code rules, not by a model’s opinion.
A duplicate “second notice” for an invoice already paid: blocked.
Every invoice gets an Ed25519-signed evidence receipt.
Change one byte and verification fails. Anyone can check it.
Eleven real attacks, run inside the same sandbox an invoice gets.
Host escape, env dump, metadata SSRF, fork bomb, memory bomb, exfiltration.
All eleven contained on the Vultr sandbox VM.
Each result names the sandbox run and container that produced it.
On 40 labelled invoices, 22 of them attacks, every outcome was right.
No false positives, and under a cent of model cost per invoice.
Airlock is for AP teams, and for AP-automation platforms adding AI agents.
It’s priced by invoice volume, and it costs under a cent in model calls per invoice.
Others process invoices or isolate code. Airlock does AP checks inside a sandbox, with a human gate.
Next: mailbox intake and ERP connectors, then the same airlock for any untrusted document.
Built on Vultr: Cloud Compute, Serverless Inference, VPC, Object Storage, Managed PostgreSQL.
We’re Team Beyonders, and this is Airlock.
